provenance: Every entry cites a Defects4REST taxonomy subtype (ST) or an RQ3 limitation class (L) (D3.1).

entries.name: Payload validation at boundaries
entries.applicability: A request body or constrained parameters (types, formats, ranges, enums).
entries.probe: Send values at and just beyond documented limits: types, formats (date, email), lengths, ranges, enums, nested fields.
entries.oracle: Valid boundary values are accepted and kept as sent; invalid ones are refused with 4xx and a message naming the field.
entries.source: Defects4REST taxonomy ST4 (data validation and transformation)

adherence.probe: A request uses a value at or beyond a documented limit.
adherence.oracle: An assertion checks acceptance with the stored value, or refusal with an error message.

entries.name: Filter and search semantics
entries.applicability: A GET with a filter or search parameter.
entries.probe: Filter on a value taken from a created or listed item, and repeat with an equivalent filter form.
entries.oracle: Every returned item satisfies the filter, the known matching item is included, and equivalent filters return the same items.

adherence.probe: A request filters on a known value.
adherence.oracle: An assertion checks that the returned items match the filter.

entries.name: Persistence round-trip
entries.applicability: A create or update with a GET on the same resource.
entries.probe: Write values for several writable fields, optional ones included, then read the resource back.
entries.oracle: Every written field reads back with exactly the written value: nothing dropped, defaulted or truncated.
entries.source: Defects4REST taxonomy ST4; limitation L1 (writes that fail to persist)

adherence.probe: A write is followed by a read of the same resource.
adherence.oracle: Assertions compare read-back fields with the written values.

entries.name: Cross-view consistency
entries.applicability: List and item views, alternate keys, or reference fields.
entries.probe: Read the same record through two views: list and item, identifier and alternate key, or by following a reference.
entries.oracle: The views agree on their shared fields, and references point to records that exist.
entries.example: GET /books → extract $[0].id and $[0].title; GET /books/{id} → $.title equals the saved title.
entries.source: Defects4REST taxonomy ST4, ST5; limitation L1

adherence.probe: The same record is read through two views.
adherence.oracle: An assertion compares a field across the views.

entries.name: Domain plausibility of values
entries.applicability: A GET that returns objects with text fields.
entries.probe: Read records and inspect values whose domain is clear from names and docs: dates, codes, amounts, statuses, names.
entries.oracle: Values fit their domain: valid date format and order, non-negative amounts, codes from the documented set, no placeholder text.

adherence.probe: Records with domain-typed fields are read.
adherence.oracle: An assertion checks a value's format, range or allowed set.

entries.name: Workflow and state transitions
entries.applicability: Action sub-resources or a create-read-update/delete lifecycle.
entries.probe: Drive the resource through a sequence of states: create, act, read; act twice; or act in a wrong state.
entries.oracle: Each step yields the documented state, invalid transitions are refused with 4xx, and a read shows the new state.
entries.example: POST /loans/{loanId}/return → GET /loans/{loanId}: $.status equals "returned"; a second return → status in [400, 409].
entries.source: Defects4REST taxonomy ST2 (state and workflow); limitation L2 (stateless testing)

adherence.probe: A sequence of state-changing requests is sent.
adherence.oracle: An assertion checks the resulting state or the refusal of an invalid step.

entries.name: Session and role variation
entries.applicability: A secured operation and a second user.
entries.probe: Run the operation as one user on another user's resource, and once with no credentials.
entries.oracle: Another user cannot read or change the resource (403 or 404), and one user's data never shows in another's response.
entries.example: GET /notes/{noteId} with auth secondary → status in [403, 404]; $.text notExists.
entries.source: Defects4REST taxonomy ST6, ST7 (authentication, authorisation); limitation L3

adherence.probe: A request is sent as a second user or without credentials.
adherence.oracle: Assertions check refusal and that no owner data is returned.

entries.name: Representation variation
entries.probe: Vary the representation: page size and offset, selected fields, sort order, and edge values (0, 1, very large).
entries.oracle: Item sets stay consistent across representations; edge values get 2xx or a clear 4xx, never 5xx or a malformed body.

adherence.oracle: An assertion checks item counts, fields or order under the variation.

entries.name: Runtime error surface
entries.probe: Send malformed or unexpected requests: unknown fields, deeply nested or oversized values, wrong content types.
entries.oracle: No 5xx; error bodies carry a message and no stack trace, SQL text or file paths.

adherence.probe: A malformed or unexpected request is sent.
adherence.oracle: Assertions exclude 5xx and check the error body for internals.

entries.name: File and storage handling
entries.probe: Upload a small file and read or list it back; also upload an empty file and one with an unusual name.
entries.oracle: The stored file keeps its name and content; invalid uploads are refused with 4xx and a message.

adherence.probe: A file is uploaded and then read back, or an invalid file is uploaded.
adherence.oracle: An assertion checks the stored file's name or content, or the refusal.
